title: Meadowgate Payments — integration scratchpad
content:
Context: Meadowgate is a mid-market payments processor (card rails + ACH) evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a decision engine that enriches transactions in real time for fraud scoring and routing. They are sensitive to PCI scope and EU data residency; target production in Q3 with a PoC in April.

Last call (2026-03-02) — attendees: Meadowgate: Claire J., Raj P., Viktor (infra). Redwood: Anika, Samir, Eleni. Call length ~45m. Quick notes below — mostly action-item oriented.

Objectives from customer:
- Validate that we can run inference on transaction payloads without bringing sensitive card data into Redwood-hosted systems. Prefer customer-managed VPC + private control plane.
- Maintain sub-75ms p95 inference for the scoring endpoint (typical payload: 80–250 tokens per request after normalization).
- Throughput target: 300 TPS sustained for baseline, with burst to 1k TPS during surges.
- Auditing + key management: HSM backed KMS, audit logs forwarded to Splunk/S3.
- Model needs: small-ish contextual model for routing + an embedding model for historical similarity (fraud pattern search).

Hard requirements flagged:
- PCI SAQ/third-party attestation required. Meadowgate will email their security questionnaire (Samir to review).
- EU residency: primary data centers in Frankfurt and Dublin. Data egress restrictions for EU cardholder data.
- No card PANs to leave their VPC — means prompts must be tokenized/hashed client-side, or we run inference fully inside their private deployment.

Technical notes + gotchas (brain dump):
- Private deployment modes: full on-prem vs Redwood Private (VPC with private control plane). Meadowgate prefers the latter for faster time-to-value, but wants option to air-gap later.
- If we accept hashed PANs as stable keys in prompts, must confirm entropy/format so model embeddings are not insecurely correlated. Security flagged this as potential fingerprinting issue.
- Tokenization differences: their payload normalization inserts delimiter markers; might change token counts vs our benchmarks. Need sample payloads to benchmark p95.
- Embeddings for fraud search: they want 1e6 historical vectors searchable with sub-150ms recall for top-10. We'll propose FAISS on their infra and embedding proxy in Redwood Private to generate vectors. Check memory footprint and shard strategy for 1M vectors (float16 vs quantized).
- Caching: prefix caching helps for templated prompts (merchant metadata). But transaction-specific fields limit cache hit rate. Consider KV cache for merchant profiles to shave 10–20ms.
- Batching policy: higher batch size improves throughput but hurts latency. For 75ms p95 target at 300 TPS, likely need dedicated GPU pool + single-request dispatch (or very small micro-batches). Estimate: a g4dn-like instance with optimized kernels may handle ~250–400 concurrent small requests depending on seq len. Need perf run.
- Model variants: suggest starting with Redwood-curated MPT-7B-q4 for scoring path (lower cost) and a larger MPT-12B-q8 for higher-sensitivity paths. We must validate ROC curve differences (FPR/FNR) on their labeled sample.

Security/compliance notes:
- KMS integration: Meadowgate uses AWS KMS + a Thales HSM appliance at the edge. They want Redwood to support customer KMS rotation windows and provide key usage logs.
- Audit trails required at transaction-id granularity; they want a log entry for each inference call (model id, latency, route, hash of inputs). This will increase log volume a lot — pricing/retention discussion needed.
- PCI scoping: Redwood on private VPC reduces scope; still need to confirm whether inference artifacts (cache, KV store) persist raw inputs in any way. Default: no raw inputs persisted. Clarify with infra team.

Cost / capacity roughing: (very rough)
- Dedicated capacity reservation: to hit 300 TPS p95-75ms with small model, ballpark 4–8 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (depends on kernel perf). For burst to 1k TPS, autoscale or burst pool required; recommend reserve baseline + burst credits.
- Storage: 1M embedding vectors (~1536 dims float16) ~1.5GB * 1e6 / ??? Wait compute properly — need to sync with infra for shard plan. (Note-to-self: compute exact size; float16 2 bytes * dims * vectors = 2 * 1536 * 1e6 = 3.072GB? That seems off — re-check offline.)

Open questions (assign):
1) Do Meadowgate accept hashing PANs client-side as effectively removing PANs from Redwood scope? -> Action: Samir to validate with Redwood Security + ask Meadowgate for their proposed hashing scheme (due 2026-03-10).
2) Sample payloads: need 1k representative payloads (sanitized) and 100 labeled fraud positives for model eval. -> Action: Meadowgate (Claire) to share by 2026-03-12.
3) EU residency: confirm whether analytics/alerts metadata may be stored in US console or needs EU-only. -> Action: Eleni to confirm with product/legal (due 2026-03-13).
4) Embeddings indexing strategy: quantization approach and retrieval infra. -> Action: Marta to draft FAISS sharding options and memory estimates (due 2026-03-18).

PoC plan (4–6 weeks):
- Week 0 (now): baseline discovery + sample data intake.
- Week 1: PoC tenant provision in Dublin, sample data ingest, baseline perf runs with synthetic payloads.
- Week 2–3: Model tuning and eval on provided labeled data; embedding pipeline test with 100k vectors subset.
- Week 4: Integration with their routing service + smoke end-to-end. Collect audit logs, latency numbers, and cost estimate.
- Decision gate: if p95 <= 75ms and FPR meets their target, move to dedicated capacity design.

API / prompt notes (examples to include in PoC):
- Example scoring call: POST /v1/score -> {"txn_id":"...","merchant_id":"...","payload_hash":"...","context":{merchant_profile}}. We must define allowed keys that contain no raw PAN/PII.
- Prompt template: "Score transaction: [MERCHANT_META] [ENCODED_TXN_FIELDS]\nReturn: score, reasons (structured array up to 3 reasons), flags". Keep structured output to allow deterministic audit extraction.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Send architect-level slide (2-pager) summarizing private deployment options + high-level TCO for baseline and burst (Anika, due 2026-03-06).
- Security scoping Q uploaded to Jira RED-1482 (Samir to review questionnaire and add comments, due 2026-03-09).
- Ask customer for sanitized sample payloads (Claire). Follow-up email template below.

Email template to send (copy/paste):
"Hi Claire — good chat earlier. Quick ask: can you share ~1k sanitized transaction payloads (remove PAN, CVV) and 100 labeled fraud-positive examples so we can run an initial model validation? Also a short doc on your proposed client-side hashing scheme for PANs if you plan to use it. We'll provision a Dublin PoC tenant and run perf tests within 1 week of receiving samples. — Anika"

Notes to self:
- Remember to highlight audit log costs to customer; they underestimate volume.
- Validate whether console exposes any preview of raw request content for debugging in private deployments; if so, we need controls.
- Perf bench ordering: request help from serving-runtime team (Samir to ping Jose in serving-runtime).

Meeting follow-ups scheduled:
- 2026-03-11: internal sync (Redwood) to assemble PoC kit (Anika/Samir/Eleni).
- 2026-03-17: PoC kickoff with Meadowgate (tentative).

Random jots:
- Consider offering quick-start script that accepts merchant CSV and returns hashed merchant profile keys + sample prompts to reduce onboarding friction.
- Could productize "PCI-shielded prompts" as a checkbox in Redwood Console (YAGNI?)

End of scratchpad.
